sections.h2: Where does Lenoir County send its property tax bills from?
sections.html:
Bills come from the Lenoir County Tax Department in the administration building at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston, phone 252-527-7174. Walk-in service runs on weekdays between 8:30 in the morning and 5:00 in the afternoon.

One office carries several jobs. It lists and appraises real estate, keeps ownership and transfer records, tracks exemptions, exclusions and deferrals, and mails the bills. It also bills the special districts layered over the county: fire districts, municipal service districts and drainage districts. Solid waste fees, privilege licenses and permits to move mobile homes run through the same counter.

The county website links to online bill viewing and payment, real property records, GIS maps, a scheduler for real property appeals, and listing forms for business and individual personal property. A seller checking a bill before closing can look there first and then phone for a payoff figure.

sections.h2: What are the due dates and interest rules on a Lenoir County bill?
sections.html:
A bill is due on September 1, yet it costs nothing extra until January 6. Interest then starts at 2 percent for the period through February 1, and 3/4 percent is added for every month or fraction after that.

Calendar rules that shape a Lenoir County tax year, with the statute for each
StepWhat the law saysWhere to read it

Checks sent by mail are credited on the postmark date.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Lenoir County property value?
sections.html:
A real estate appeal in Lenoir County goes to the Board of Equalization and Review. Its 2026 window ended April 23, 2026, the day the board adjourned, and the county says the 2027 window opens January 1, 2027.

This quasi-judicial board hears disputes over how real estate and personal property were listed and appraised, plus exemption applications, exclusion requests and present-use classifications, all under G.S. 105-322.

The rule on timing is that a hearing must be requested, in writing or in person, before the board adjourns. A written decision follows within 30 days of adjournment. Someone still unhappy can file notice with the state Property Tax Commission inside 30 days of the mailing date, stating the grounds and sending a copy to the assessor. The county site offers a form for scheduling a real property appeal.

sections.h2: When did Lenoir County last revalue property?
sections.html:
Lenoir County's own page says assessed values held steady after the reappraisal effective January 1, 2017, and it described the next one as effective January 1, 2025. North Carolina law sets the outside limit at eight years between reappraisals of real property.

In between, a value changes only when the property does, for example through new construction or a removed building. During a reappraisal, certified appraisers visit parcels, confirm characteristics and study sales and costs so every property is measured as of the same date.

An assessed figure is not a price. Compare your notice with recent sales before setting an asking price, and ask the tax office for the current assessed value on your parcel.

sections.h2: What property tax relief programs exist for Lenoir County owners?
sections.html:
Three homestead programs exist statewide, and the county takes the AV-9 application for them. An owner can use only one program. File during the listing period; the county must still accept an application up to June 1 before the tax year.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the larger of $25,000 or half the home's appraised value, for an owner who is 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled and whose income is within the limit, printed as $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 off appraised value, with no age or income test, using Form NCDVA-9 filed with the assessor.
  • Circuit breaker: a ceiling of 4.0 percent of income for owners at or under the income limit, or 5.0 percent for incomes above it up to 150 percent of it. The owner must have lived in the home five years, and must reapply annually.

Farm, horticulture and forest land may qualify for present-use value, which lowers the assessment. Lenoir County has an AV-7 form to request an estimate of deferred taxes, a useful step before selling qualifying land.

sections.h2: What happens to Lenoir County property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The lien reaches a parcel on its January 1 listing date, so the unpaid balance travels with the house. At closing, the attorney or title company usually requests the figure from the Lenoir County Tax Department and pays it out of the seller's proceeds.

Personal property works differently. A lien for unpaid personal property tax can reach every parcel the taxpayer owns in that taxing unit, so an old boat or equipment bill may surface against a house. Boats, jet skis, aircraft, mobile homes and unlicensed vehicles are listed each January, with a 10 percent penalty for a late listing.

Real estate follows a permanent listing system in this county. A seller does not relist the house every year unless its value changed.

sections.h2: What happens if Lenoir County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The county can sue to foreclose its tax lien, a process modeled on mortgage foreclosure and filed in the county where the property sits. Owners of record, spouses and other lienholders receive notice.

A sale is held at the courthouse door to the highest bidder. The commissioner can ask for a deposit as high as 20 percent of the bid and reports the sale in three days. Parties have 10 days after the report to file exceptions or a higher bid, and the commissioner's fee may reach 5 percent of the price. Until confirmation, an owner can redeem by paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

The county tax page names a legal services contact for tax foreclosures. Anyone holding a notice should call the tax office and a legal aid provider promptly.

sections.h2: What are the housing and income figures for Lenoir County?
sections.html:
Kinston's county had an estimated 55,837 residents on July 1, 2025, down from 59,495 in the 2010 census, and it has 27,402 housing units across 399.09 square miles.

Census survey figures for 2020 to 2024 put the typical owned home at $120,500, with owners in 59.2 percent of homes and renters in the rest, at a median gross rent of $861. Households earn a median $45,143. Poverty affects 19.1 percent of residents, and 22.4 percent are 65 or older.

Monthly owner costs are a median $1,237 with a mortgage and $460 without one. At home values this modest, a tax bill is a real share of yearly housing cost, and back taxes can eat much of a house's equity. Permits numbered 131 in 2025, so new construction is thin and a resale competes mostly with other older homes.

faqs.q: Which phone number reaches Lenoir County tax staff?
faqs.a: Dial 252-527-7174. The Tax Department sits at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston and keeps hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: Is the Lenoir County real estate appeal period still open for 2026?
faqs.a: No. It closed April 23, 2026, when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourned. The county says the window for 2027 opens January 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Must a Lenoir County homeowner list the house each year?
faqs.a: No. The county runs a permanent listing system for real estate, so a house is relisted only after a change in value. Boats, aircraft and unlicensed vehicles need a January listing.

faqs.q: What does a late personal property listing cost in Lenoir County?
faqs.a: A 10 percent penalty. Listings made after the period ending January 31 are charged it, per the county tax page.

faqs.q: Can a house with unpaid Lenoir County tax be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax lien is paid out of the sale proceeds at closing. Get the balance from the tax office before signing so the payoff appears on the settlement statement.
